questions.q: What dataset does Project 1 use, and where was it first introduced in this course?
options: Sample Superstore, first established in Lesson 3 and used throughout the course
AdventureWorks2012, from the T-SQL Development course
A brand-new dataset created specifically for this project
Northwind, a sample e-commerce database
questions.explain: Project 1 builds on Sample Superstore, the same dataset this course has used since Lesson 3 — the project applies skills learned throughout, not a new unfamiliar dataset.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend coloring the sales-by-region map by Profit Ratio rather than raw Sales?
options: Profit Ratio shows where the business is actually healthy, not just where it happens to be large
Tableau does not allow maps to be colored by Sales
Profit Ratio is easier to calculate than Sales
Raw Sales cannot be used with geographic roles
questions.explain: A region can have high Sales but poor profitability — coloring by Profit Ratio tells a more useful executive story than raw Sales volume alone.

questions.q: What is described as the single most important technical requirement of this project?
options: A working filter action connecting the map to the trend line and top-10 chart
Using at least five different chart types
Publishing the dashboard to Tableau Server before it's finished
Using a live connection instead of an extract
questions.explain: The filter action is what turns four separate charts into one connected, interactive dashboard — the lesson calls this out as the most important requirement.

questions.q: According to the rubric, how should the top-10-products chart be built?
options: With an actual Top N filter, sorted descending and labeled — not a manually curated list
By manually selecting ten products the author thinks look good
By showing all products and letting the viewer scroll to find the top ten
By using a data-driven alert instead of a filter
questions.explain: A strong version uses a real Top N filter so the ranking is dynamic and correct, rather than a hand-picked, static list.

questions.q: What separates a 'passable' version of this dashboard from a 'strong' one, according to the lesson?
options: Details like a reliably working filter action and deliberate color encoding — not simply having a sixth chart
The number of sheets included in the dashboard
Whether it was built in Tableau Cloud instead of Tableau Desktop
How many calculated fields it contains
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states the difference is in execution details — a flaky filter action or default, meaningless coloring — not in adding more charts.
